title: Review OCR suspect queues, starting with Challenger
description: Review the 999 open OCR suspects through each report's fidelity workflow. Start with challenger-accident, the largest and messiest queue; record either a deterministic correction or a dismissal so each reviewed suspect leaves the queue permanently.
acceptance_criteria: Review Challenger suspects against the source PDF; record each outcome in the report-owned correction/dismissal data; run the report's prescribed ingestion and fidelity checks; inspect rendered output; leave an updated queue count.
notes:
2026-09-07 — Challenger body pass (PDF pp. 1–200), reviewed against the source scan.

Queue: 371 open → 345 open (7 → 33 judged correct).

corrections.yaml in ../challenger-accident:
- 12 corrections (c-0001..c-0012): 8× 'Recomrnendation/Recornmendat(ion)/Recornmendations' → 'Recommendation(s)' (rn→m OCR of the report's own section headings, narrowed by printed page where the token recurs); 'Cornmission'/'Cornmiasion' → 'Commission' (footnote citations of the Rogers Commission report); 'returnng' → 'returning'; stripped ' lVlll' (mis-OCR of the Contents-page number 'viii').
- 26 dismissals: common English words flagged only for an rn/m sequence (concerns, warning, morning, California, alternatives, preburner(s), …) and two line-break tails already rejoined in the output (cerns→concerns, ternal→External).

Verified: pnpm ingest verify (all fidelity checks green), pnpm ingest check + pnpm ingest baseline challenger-accident (output moved -2 words, baseline accepted), pnpm corpus check (challenger unchanged — no citable id moved), pnpm prerender + grep of rendered HTML (no leftover garble; corrected forms present).

Split out: reportsthatmatter-9zk — the 'Recommendation' headings still merge into the previous paragraph in ~6 places; that's an @rtm/ingest heading-detection bug, not a per-line correction.

Remaining in Challenger (~345): footnote-apparatus garble in pp. 48–200 (mangled footnote numbers / 'Ibid' — 2o, 1bid, 2T, I6Ibid, …), region C appendix prose (pp. 201–260, ~33), region D appendix tables/memos/distribution lists (pp. 261+, ~274 — heavily degraded; many are correct-as-printed alphanumeric part/equipment/document codes). Recommend a dedicated follow-up: a rule/pass to bulk-classify the correct-as-printed codes, then a scoped human pass on what's left, rather than 274 one-off judgements on near-illegible scans. Other reports' queues not yet started.
Corpus blast radius (pnpm corpus check): 9 paragraph permalinks moved in challenger, all direct consequences of the fixes — 'recomrnendation'→'recommendation', '78-rogers-cornmission-report-volume'→'…commission…', 'rogers-cornmiasion-report-volume-i'→'…commission…', and ~5 collision-suffix bumps where the corrected words join an existing 'Recommendation(s)'/'Rogers Commission Report' dedup series. Read the diff; accepted with 'pnpm corpus accept challenger-accident'. ./scripts/verify.sh now exits 0 (All checks passed). challenger-accident is not R2-pinned, and the moved ids were OCR-garble slugs.
2026-09-11 — Challenger footnote-apparatus pass (PDF pp. 48-200 remainder), reviewed against the source scan — several confirmed by rendering the actual page image (pdftoppm), not just the text layer.

Queue: 337 open -> 310 open (41 -> 68 judged correct). Region A (PDF <=47, the Committee's own findings/recommendations) is now fully clear (0 open) after the earlier bookkeeping fix. Region B (footnotes+narrative, 48-200) reduced from 46 to 4 open.

19 corrections (c-0013..c-0033, skipping c-0015/c-0030 — see below): mostly footnote-number reconstructions, verified by bracketing (a garbled number sitting between two clean ones, e.g. '2T'->27 between 26 and 28) or by matching a clean inline citation elsewhere on the page (e.g. 'lZ3Douglas'->123Douglas, matching an already-clean '123' inline). Several needed the actual page image to resolve safely rather than guess: 'lZo'/'lZ4'-family digits are NOT a fixed cipher for this OCR run — '1Z' turned out to be '17' (not '12', my first guess from a wrongly-assumed Z->2 pattern), caught only by rendering the page.

19 dismissals of the newly-corrected match strings (queue bookkeeping — a correction alone never retires a suspect from the queue; see the note above c-0013 in corrections.yaml) + 8 real dismissals (D6AC, 2nd, 1D, 2G, 5B, 6th, 7th — all real words/codes, and '1s' — a Figure VI-2 axis label confirmed '15' against the page image but embedded in an otherwise-illegible ASCII-art diagram).

Real finding: corrections.yaml cannot reach footnote-*definition* text (the rendered '[^N]: ...' blocks) — only body paragraphs/quotes/lists. Confirmed empirically. Two otherwise-solved fixes (footnote 11 '1bid'->'11 Ibid.', and footnote 6's editorial note 'iNm'->'[NOTE.-...]') are left open because of this, both verified correct against the page image but structurally unreachable. Filed as reportsthatmatter-3jb.

Also found and left open: 'lZo' at PDF p.142 sits inside a hyphen-rejoin/footnote-fusion parser bug ('essen-' + the page's footnote text got glued into one fake word 'essenlZo' with no hyphen or space) — a parser issue, not a text correction, in the spirit of reportsthatmatter-9zk. And a THIRD, different 'lZ4' occurrence was spotted in the rendered output (printed p.245-ish, Launch Commit Criteria) that isn't part of this batch's review — left untouched, noted for a future pass.

Verified: pnpm ingest verify (green), pnpm ingest check + baseline (output moved: -1 paragraph/+1 word, from a footnote reference becoming properly linked once its number was fixed; read and accepted), pnpm corpus check + accept (8 paragraph ids moved, all direct/expected consequences, read and accepted), pnpm prerender + grep of rendered HTML (no leftover garble from this batch; corrected forms present). ./scripts/verify.sh green.

Remaining in Challenger (~310): region C appendix prose (~33) and region D appendix tables/memos/distribution lists (~274, mostly correct-as-printed codes per the earlier recommendation) still untouched. Not yet committed to main/published — sitting on local changes pending the user's go-ahead, same as the first batch.

title: Give every page a real social preview image (og:image), not just 5 curated quotes
description:
Right now almost nothing on the site has a social-preview image. og:image is only advertised for the handful of curated quotes in docs/share-quotes.yaml (docs/v2-features.yaml's 'quote-cards' feature, deliberately scoped that way: 'an og:image pointing at a 404 is worse than no image at all'). Everything else — the homepage (src/templates/index.ts renderLayout call passes no options at all), /reports, every report's contents page, every section page, and any paragraph link that isn't one of the ~5 curated quotes — falls back to a bare text preview (twitter:card=summary, no image) when shared to Slack, iMessage, X, etc. For a project whose whole point is getting these reports shared and read, a text-only preview on nearly every link is a real gap, not a cosmetic one.

Related but distinct: GH issue #99 ('Imagery: study Co-Star's visual language, then give every report a mark') is about each report's visual identity/branding, not specifically about making every page's share preview non-empty. Worth reading together, not the same task.
acceptance_criteria: Every page type has a real, reachable og:image (homepage/site default, each report's own default card, and ideally section/paragraph-level where a curated one doesn't exist) — verified by checking the rendered <meta property="og:image"> on a sample of pages (/, a report /full page, a report contents page, an uncurated paragraph link) actually resolves (200, not 404). Reuses the existing card.ts/cards.mjs rendering machinery (renderCard, pnpm cards) rather than a parallel mechanism. Design pass on what a 'default' card looks like (site-wide vs per-report) before building it.
notes:
2026-09-11 — Shipped and verified live.

Design: a second card layout, renderDefaultCard (src/templates/card.ts) — title + subtitle, no quote, same visual language as the existing quote cards (mark, off-white canvas, serif headline, mono chrome). Generated via scripts/cards.mjs: one per report (title + byline) and one for the site itself (homepage's own headline/standfirst, pulled from a new shared src/templates/site.ts so the card copy can't drift from the page).

Fallback chain (cheapest/most specific first): curated paragraph card -> report's own default card -> site card. shareImage() (report.ts, exported, shared with section.ts) handles the first two; renderHead (layout.ts) supplies the site card as the unconditional floor every page lands on when it passes no image at all -- so a future page that forgets to wire one in still gets something, by construction, not by every call site remembering.

11 new PNGs committed (1.1MB, ~100-145KB each): assets/cards/site.png + assets/cards/<report-id>/default.png x10.

Verified live on production across all four fallback tiers: homepage -> site card, a report contents page (challenger-accident) -> report card, an uncurated paragraph (jack-smith-vol1) -> report card, a curated paragraph -> still its specific quote card, /about -> site card. VERIFY_BASE=https://reportsthatmatter.org ./scripts/verify.sh green.

Shipped: main (commit aa08be1), deployed. Logged: docs/CHANGELOG.md + reportsthatmatter/visual-changelog (2026-09-11-social-preview-cards/, 3 images).

Acceptance criteria met. Closing.
close_reason: Every page type now has a real, reachable og:image, verified live on production across all fallback tiers (site/report/curated-quote). Shipped, deployed, logged.

title: Make per-chapter footnote identities safe for Leveson
description: Leveson restarts footnote numbering by chapter, while the ingestion pipeline treats a number as report-global. Correct identity and rendering without making marker-linking unsafe.
acceptance_criteria: Every rendered Leveson footnote reference resolves to its own chapter-local definition; no output exceeds deployment asset limits; ingestion checks and rendered-page inspection confirm the result.
notes:
2026-09-11 — Fixed upstream in @rtm/ingest (v0.12.4), verified against real Leveson data, shipped corpus-wide.

Root cause: renderEndnotes/collectNotes/withSidenotes modelled a footnote's identity as its bare number, deduping/looking up by number alone. Any report where two genuinely different notes share a number -- Leveson's deliberate per-chapter restart, or (discovered along the way) OCR misreading a footnote marker's digits so it collides with an unrelated earlier note -- collapsed those notes into one merged definition, and every reference to that number resolved to whichever text won the collapse.

Fix: reference markers are untouched (no change to where/how a [^N] gets written). Definition RESOLUTION is now position-aware: renderEndnotes still merges adjacent same-number entries (exact repeats, page-break tails -- unchanged, same tests pass), but non-adjacent same-number entries stay separate definitions; collectNotes returns all of a number's definitions in document order; withSidenotes resolves each [^N] reference against them positionally (1st reference -> 1st definition, 2nd -> 2nd, ...). New unit + integration tests in @rtm/ingest (243 total passing). Tagged v0.12.4.

Real-data impact was much bigger than the bead described -- this wasn't Leveson-only. Re-ingesting under the fix moved 7 of 10 reports' footnote text (challenger-accident, columbia-accident, jack-smith-vol1, litvinenko-inquiry, uk-leveson-inquiry, us-deepwater-horizon, us-psi-financial-crisis), all verified by direct comparison: body text byte-for-byte identical in every case, only the Notes section changed, growing as merged blobs split back into correct definitions. us-deepwater-horizon was hit hardest -- 1,226 sidenotes, same count before and after, but the rendered page shrank 2.07MB -> 1.78MB because each sidenote now shows only its own text instead of a shared merged blob. All 10 reports pass pnpm ingest verify/check; pnpm corpus check diffs read and accepted (6 reports: footnote-only, zero citable-paragraph impact, confirmed by identical body byte-count; Leveson: real paragraph-id moves too, see below).

Leveson specifically: its own package.json was still pinned to v0.2.1 (never updated since migration), ~10 versions behind. Bumping it to get this fix meant adopting everything else the pipeline gained since too -- footnote recall in particular (8,605 footnotes now found vs the old ~1,680, most previously merged). This DOES move real Leveson paragraph-id citations (23 sections affected, mostly from a few headings losing a spurious 'CHAPTER' prefix that had been concatenating into the section title). Read and accepted deliberately -- see uk-leveson-inquiry's own commit (8fbc371) for the full account. Asset size checked explicitly given the bead's #103 history: full-body.html is 8.9MB, safely under the 25 MiB Cloudflare limit.

Verified via rendered-page inspection (the acceptance criteria's own requirement): of 62 Leveson footnote numbers with more than one resolved occurrence in the final HTML, all 62 now show correctly distinct text -- was effectively 0/63 correct on an earlier, not-yet-fully-baselined check.

Split off, not attempted here: reportsthatmatter-axw (linkInlineMarkers still links some non-footnote numbers -- a few dates, a repeated boilerplate block with a likely-dropped phone-number leading zero -- a pre-existing, separate defect that predates this fix and doesn't dominate the corpus the way the identity bug did, but is visible in spot checks).

Shipped: @rtm/ingest v0.12.4 (tagged, released); all 7 affected report repos on main/master; site repo pin bumped, all 10 reports aggregated, corpus-baseline.json accepted. ./scripts/verify.sh green throughout, multiple times, including after every baseline-accept round.
close_reason: Fixed upstream in @rtm/ingest v0.12.4, verified against real Leveson data (62/62 repeated footnote numbers now resolve to correct, distinct text), and shipped corpus-wide -- 7 of 10 reports had the same underlying bug (footnote definitions merging across unrelated notes when numbers collide), all re-ingested and verified. Residual, separate false-positive-linking issue split off to reportsthatmatter-axw.

title: linkInlineMarkers over-links dates and counts as footnote references (Leveson: dates like '11,[^13] and 19 March' )
description:
Discovered while fixing reportsthatmatter-ooj (per-chapter footnote identity) and inspecting real Leveson output after the fix. linkInlineMarkers (@rtm/ingest src/footnotes.ts) converts a bare digit after punctuation+space into a [^N] reference whenever N is a footnote number ANYWHERE in the document. In an 8000+-footnote document like Leveson, virtually every number 1-999 is 'known' somewhere, so the check is nearly no filter at all. Real examples pulled from Leveson's rendered output:

  'On,[^13] July 2011' (should read 'On 13 July 2011' -- 13 is a day-of-month, not a footnote)
  'three telephone calls made on 11,[^13] and 19 March 2003' (11 and 19 are also dates; only 13 happened to collide with a real footnote number and got linked)
  'officers were charged and prosecuted,[^13] were found guilty' (13 is a count)
  'on three occasions:[^13] June 2010,[^13] August 2010' (dates again)
  'Telephone orders:[^20] 7219 3890' (repeated 'Houses of Parliament Shop' order-form boilerplate, 4 occurrences x 3 numbers each -- likely a dropped leading zero from a '020' phone prefix)

reportsthatmatter-ooj's fix makes each [^N] reference resolve to a definition positionally, in the order references and definitions appear -- correct when references are genuine, but these false-positive markers consume 'slots' in that ordering too, so they can misalign the resolution for genuine references of the same number that come after them in the same chapter. Real impact measured: of 63 footnote numbers in Leveson with more than one resolved occurrence, only 2 showed genuinely different (correct) text after the identity fix; the other 61 still showed one shared text, dominated by false-positive links like the ones above rather than genuine chapter restarts.

This is a pre-existing defect, not introduced by reportsthatmatter-ooj's fix -- before that fix these same false markers already showed some (wrong) footnote text, just less visibly so since everything of a given number collapsed into one blob anyway.
acceptance_criteria: linkInlineMarkers (or a stronger guard on it) stops linking day-of-month and small-count numbers that happen to share a value with a real footnote number, verified against the specific Leveson examples above and by re-running pnpm ingest verify across the corpus with no fidelity regression. A reasonable approach: require page-local corroboration the way linkFlushMarkers/notesNear already does (a candidate is only linked if a note with that number was actually collected near this page), rather than the current document-global 'is N known anywhere' check.

title: Detect OCR-mangled section headings in Challenger (Recommendation/Finding merged into prior paragraph)
description: In challenger-accident, the report's own division headings ('Recommendation', 'Recommendations', and in places 'Finding'/'Issue') are frequently NOT detected as headings and instead get reflowed onto the end of the preceding body paragraph — e.g. '...some of these past problems have been corrected while others have not. Recommendation'. Root cause is upstream of the corrections pass: when OCR mangled the heading word (e.g. 'Recomrnendation'), heading detection failed and a short trailing line merged into the paragraph. corrections.yaml c-0001..c-0008 (2026-09-07) repair the mangled tokens themselves, so the words now read correctly, but the heading break is still missing wherever the merge already happened (printed pp. 15, 28, 29, 33, 101, 135; two standalone cases pp. 19, 175 render fine).
acceptance_criteria: Challenger's 'Recommendation(s)' section headings render as headings, not as a sentence tail on the previous paragraph. Fix belongs in @rtm/ingest heading detection (or a short-line de-merge), not in per-line corrections. pnpm ingest check + pnpm corpus check green; affected pages inspected in the rendered output.

title: Establish a safe extraction path for FCIC digits
description: FCIC's text layer silently loses every digit. Find a trustworthy extraction path and add a corpus-level detector so this failure is visible before publication.
acceptance_criteria: FCIC digits are preserved or the report remains explicitly unpublished; a digit-loss detector fails on a representative broken input; fidelity and rendered-output review demonstrate the chosen path is safe.

title: Make remote D1 search-index application reliable
description: The documented wrangler D1 remote file import failed with Cloudflare authentication error 10000 although remote commands authenticated. Establish and document a reliable remote index-application path.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh remote search-index SQL file applies successfully with documented credentials and command; production search is checked against the newly indexed content; the deployment instructions accurately describe the working command.
notes:
2026-09-11 — fixed and automated.

Root cause: the earlier auth error 10000 was hit applying the whole-corpus file (~17 MB, all 10 reports' DELETE+INSERT in one wrangler d1 execute --remote --file=). Scoping index-search to one report (pnpm index-search <id>, new optional arg) produces an ~800 KB file for Challenger that applied cleanly via 'wrangler d1 execute reportsthatmatter-marks --remote --file=' — confirmed working, twice, no auth error. Splitting by report is the reliability fix, not just a speed-up.

Shipped:
- scripts/index-search.mjs: optional <id> arg scopes the build to one report -> build/search-index.<id>.sql
- scripts/reindex-search.sh <id> [--local]: builds + applies one report's index (documented working command)
- scripts/publish-report.mjs: now calls reindex-search.sh automatically after a successful commit (skipped on localhost, --rollback, or --no-reindex) -- so a normal publish no longer needs a separate manual search-sync step
- Documented in AGENTS.md (publish section) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (Search section + diagram)

Verified against production: challenger-accident's search_index_versions.content_version now matches the just-built index (bc147b311e00), and /search no longer surfaces the old garbled OCR text.

Remaining gap, split to reportsthatmatter-cpk: rtm-publish (self-publish from a report's own repo) doesn't trigger this yet -- it lives in the separate @rtm/ingest repo -- and nothing reads search_index_versions back to alert on staleness (so a report published any other way can still drift silently).
Correction: the follow-up bead is reportsthatmatter-9j2, not -cpk (typo'd before it was created).
close_reason: Fixed: scoping index-search + reindex-search.sh to one report resolved the remote-apply auth failure, and publish-report.mjs now runs it automatically after every publish. Remaining gaps split to reportsthatmatter-cpk.

title: Recover structural headings for Hillsborough
description: Hillsborough headings are expressed by colour and weight, not textual syntax, so pdftotext flattens them into body text and sections are poorly structured.
acceptance_criteria: The report declares any needed report-specific extraction knowledge; section headings and contents become meaningful; all fidelity gates pass; rendered sections and full view are visually inspected.

title: corrections.yaml cannot reach footnote-definition text (only body paragraphs/quotes/lists)
description: Discovered while reviewing Challenger's footnote-apparatus OCR suspects (reportsthatmatter-agk, 2026-09-11). applyCorrections' find/replace only searches paragraph/quote/list body blocks; text inside a rendered footnote-definition block (the '[^N]: ...' lines) is never reachable, confirmed empirically — plain unambiguous substrings that visibly exist in that exact rendered text never match as a correction find, while the same text matches fine when it happens to sit in ordinary body prose instead. Two confirmed-correct fixes in Challenger could not be applied because of this: footnote 11 ('1bid' -> '11 Ibid.', PDF p.62) and footnote 6's editorial note ('iNm' -> '[NOTE.-The nozzle...]', PDF p.61), both verified word-for-word against the page image.
acceptance_criteria: Either corrections.yaml gains a documented way to target footnote-definition text (a new scope, or applyCorrections searches Footnote[] too), or the limitation is documented clearly enough that reviewers stop losing time on it. The two Challenger fixes above land once fixed.

title: rtm-publish self-publish doesn't reindex search; no staleness alert on search_index_versions
description:
Two related gaps left after reportsthatmatter-7np's fix (per-report scoped reindex, auto-triggered from pnpm publish-report):

1. rtm-publish (@rtm/ingest's report-repo self-publish CLI, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md / AGENTS.md path 1) commits straight to R2+D1 but does not call anything equivalent to scripts/reindex-search.sh. A report published that way can go stale in search with nothing to notice. Fixing this belongs in @rtm/ingest (a separate repo/release), or this repo could poll report_versions and reindex whatever changed.
2. search_index_versions (D1) records which content_version was indexed per report, but nothing reads it back. There is no check anywhere (not verify.sh, not a route) that compares it against a report's actual current content and flags drift.
acceptance_criteria: Either rtm-publish reindexes search itself, or a scheduled/CI check compares search_index_versions against each report's live content_hash/prerendered state and surfaces any report that has drifted (e.g. as a verify.sh check or a /health-style endpoint).

title: Address remaining footnote recall and heading-quality cases
description: Work through the bounded ingestion-quality remainder: missing footnote links, PSI truncated headings, and heading ambiguity where it harms a report.
acceptance_criteria: Each adopted fix belongs in the pipeline or report declaration, has a failing case before the fix, passes fidelity and corpus checks after re-ingestion, and has been checked on rendered pages.
